summary_full:
Denver Broncos at Kansas City Chiefs.

BlueChip leans DEN. +++ DEN — Passing offense vs pass defense

Why DEN has the edge
- +++ DEN — Passing offense vs pass defense
- ++ DEN — Pass rush / protection (proxy)
- + DEN — Overall efficiency

BlueChip projection
Market: KC -3.0
BCW desk μ (home): +1.8 (Research Preview)
Win probability: unavailable until probability model passes validation.

How each team wins
KC: Lean on rushing offense vs run defense. Convert that mismatch before the game becomes a coin-flip script.
DEN: Attack via passing offense vs pass defense and keep the favorite from playing its preferred script.

What changed this week
• Kansas City Chiefs HC Andy Reid provides concerning update on DE Ashton Gillotte after latest training camp injury - A to Z Sports
• Kansas City Chiefs' latest roster move swaps longshot offensive linemen as injuries stack up at training camp - A to Z Sports
• Kansas City Chiefs Star Player Carted Off Field After Suffering Concerning Injury - Yahoo Sports
• Broncos add veteran safety Taylor Rapp with LB Levelle Bailey waived after injury - The Denver Post

What could make BlueChip wrong?
• Turnovers: the projection assumes roughly normal luck; a +2 swing can flip a DEN lean.
• KC path: if rushing offense vs run defense plays up, DEN's edge shrinks.
• Injury / inactive surprise on either OL or QB would rewrite the pass-rush signal.

Bottom line: DEN has more ways to win on the current MATCHUP SIGNAL board, but football variance (turnovers, explosives) remains large around any margin estimate.

glossary.EPA/play: Expected Points Added estimates how much each play improves expected scoring position. Positive is good. A 5-yard gain on 3rd-and-3 is not treated like 5 yards on 3rd-and-20.
glossary.MATCHUP SIGNAL: A descriptive strength×weakness edge. Not a published win probability and not fed into BCW-RIDGE-v0.1 until validated walk-forward.
glossary.Research Preview: BlueChip quantitative layer that has not cleared the five public ship gates.
